extracted.intended_audience: Public Information Officers (PIOs) assigned to All-Hazards Incident Management Teams, Assistant PIOs, and personnel seeking Type 3/4 AHIMT credentials or PIO training
extracted.subtask_description: A five-day instructor-led course preparing Public Information Officers to perform PIO duties within All-Hazards Incident Management Teams (AHIMTs) and local IMTs, combining basic and advanced information-function elements and assessed via exercises and a final exam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course learning outcomes — core PIO skills and AHIMT application
rubrics_metrics.description: This course will help participants develop a strong set of core PIO skills and the ability to apply them within the context of an AHIMT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on fundamental duties and responsibilities of the PIO in an all-hazards environment; intended to enable participants to both learn core skills and apply them operationally during incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course scope — integrates basic and advanced information functions
rubrics_metrics.description: This course is distinct from other information function courses in that it combines elements from both the basic and advanced functions to concentrate training on the fundamental duties and responsibilities of the PIO in an all-hazards environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course material does not assume or require experience as a PIO, but also is not a basic PIO course — i.e., intermediate/position-specific focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional methods / pedagogy
rubrics_metrics.description: This course is an instructor-led training that supports learning through discussion, lecture, and active participation in multiple exercises that provides a realistic, scenario-driven approach to mastering the skills required of a PIO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses scenario-driven exercises, discussions, lectures, and active participation to support application of knowledge in realistic incident contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment methods — exercises, simulations, and final exam
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercises, simulations, discussions, and a final exam enable participants to process and apply their new knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical performance in exercises and simulations plus a final exam are used to assess mastery of course objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience / suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: NIMS ICS All-Hazards training should be completed by personnel who are regularly assigned to Functional, Support, or Unit Leader positions on Type 3 or 4 AHIMTs, or by those persons who desire to seek credentials/certification in those positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also intended for a PIO assigned to an incident as a member of an AHIMT and local IMTs, and for Assistant PIOs in a variety of capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required prerequisites / enrollment eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Required Pre-requisites: E/G0300, ICS-300: Intermediate Incident Command System for Expanding Incidents; E/G0400, ICS-400: Advanced Incident Command System for Command and General Staff—Complex Incidents; IS-0100.b, Introduction to the Incident Command System, ICS-100; IS-0200.b, Incident Command System for Single Resources and Initial Action Incidents; IS-0700.a, National Incident Management System, An Introduction; and IS-0800.b, National Response Framework, An Introduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion of the listed ICS and NIMS foundation courses is required prior to taking this position-specific course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration / time commitment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full five-day attendance (31 hours) is implied for successful completion and credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials: NIMS ICS All-Hazards Public Information Officer Training Manual; Scenario handouts; EMSI All Hazards Public Information Officer (PIO) Job Aid (optional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary manual and scenario handouts are used for instruction; an optional job aid is available for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing education / academic credit
rubrics_metrics.description: CEUs: 3.5; ACE: Level: Lower Division/Associate; ACE: Credit Hours: 2; ACE: Curriculum: Emergency Management or Public Administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies continuing education units and ACE college-credit equivalency and curricular alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program area alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Area(s): Citizen Preparedness; Incident Command System; Universal Emergency Preparedness; FEMA Employee Training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course aligns with multiple FEMA program areas and is positioned within national preparedness and ICS training frameworks.
